question: Which of the following does not come under the power of the Governor of a State in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Obligatory power**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Constitution of India, the Governor has executive, legislative and judicial powers.
 
• The executive power helps the Governor in performing the functions of the state government.
 
• The Governor can exercise discretionary power independently under special circumstances.
 
• Under the legislative power, the Governor can convene meetings of the legislature and issue ordinances.
 
• Compulsory power is not included in the powers of the Governor, as no such power has been given in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Executive Power:** The Governor is the head of the state executive and acts on the advice of the State Council of Ministers.
 
• **Legislative Power:** The Governor has the power to convene, adjourn and dissolve the Assembly.
 
• **Discretionary Power:** The Governor can take decisions independently without the advice of the State Council of Ministers in certain matters.
 
• **Judicial Power:** The Governor has the power to decide on mercy petitions.
 
• **Constitutional Power:** The Governor takes an oath to protect and preserve the Constitution and ensure that it is followed in the state.
